concepts.def: Spaniards marry later and divorce more, and single-parent and blended families - familias monoparentales y reconstituidas - are increasingly common.
Spain has one of the lowest birth rates in Europe, with parenthood postponed for economic and work-related reasons.
Spain legalised same-sex marriage in 2005, among the first countries in the world to do so.
Key issues include el paro (unemployment), especially el paro juvenil, los contratos temporales and the growth of el teletrabajo.
Tourism is a pillar of the Spanish economy and Spain is among the world's most visited countries, but mass tourism strains coasts, cities and housing.
Debates on gender equality at work centre on la brecha salarial (the pay gap) and la conciliación between family and working life.

Theme 1: Evolution of Spanish Society — a core area of A-Level Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 1: Evolution of Spanish Society brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.
